text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager triggered: 'router-p99-latency-spike' — p99 > 2s across US-W regions, streaming stalls observed. Bridge: https://calls.re/redwood/6177770000

sam: seeing p95 ~400ms but p99 jumping to 2.2-3s, streaming sessions dropouts for ~30s windows. Customers report 'long pauses' in streaming.

lia: alerted from perf dashboards — high tail on router egress latencies, LB weights look noisy. adding logs now.

mike: oncall here, joining bridge. any initial hypotheses?

jake: early glance: routing policy agent pushed a weight roll earlier (09:12 UTC) to prefer region-local. I see sudden hotshard signals after that.

mitra: confirming — policy rollout id 2026-09-15-rl-27. It updated peer affinity rules -> increased stickiness to some shards. Could create hot partitions.

emily: customer impact: 3 enterprise customers reported 5xxs and streaming stalls in last 10m. Triage: likely SLO breaches for a subset of requests.

sam: logs:```
ERROR router::dispatch::hotkey "shard=shard-42" tail_latency_ms=2400 route_weight=0.87
WARN lb::conn "zone=usw2" queue_length=180
```

mike: can we roll back the policy? Is it safe?

jake: we can rollback quickly to previous policy id 2026-09-15-rl-26 with zero-downtime. but we should consider an intermediate throttle to avoid oscillation.

lia: telemetry shows load concentrated to shard-42 and shard-43 in usw2. Affected requests correlated with long-sequence streaming jobs (avg token seq_len > 800). KV cache miss rate up on those nodes.

mitra: plan: 1) flip policy rollback 2) enable eager-fallback to smaller instance pool for streaming 3) bump eviction thresholds for hotkey detection 4) monitor p99s for 10m.

mike: do it. Jake can you run rollback now?

jake: running rollback command:```
# rollback routing policy
rdctl rollout revert --policy-id=2026-09-15-rl-27 --target-id=2026-09-15-rl-26 --force
```

jake: rollback submitted at 09:21:12 UTC. Watching control plane events.

incident-bot: Rollback job 7781 started. ETA ~45s. Updates in thread.

lia: while that's happening, I'm toggling eager-fallback for streaming routes to route to compatible quantized variants to reduce per-token cost and reduce latency.

mitra: also temporarily increasing hotkey eviction to 5% to avoid thrashing during rollback.

emily: sending customers a short notice: "We're investigating increased latency in streaming; mitigation underway. We'll update in 15 minutes."

sam: :eyes: p99 trending down from 3.1s -> 1.4s after 90s from rollback start. p95 stable. streaming stall reports drop to near-zero.

mike: nice. are any nodes still showing queue spikes?

lia: shard-42 queue length falling from 180 -> 25 over 3 minutes. KV-cache hit recovering.

jake: rollback finished at 09:22:05 UTC. policy reverted. Confirmed no errors in apply.

mitra: enabling automatic fallback policy to legacy routing for the streaming namespace for 30 minutes to smooth traffic.```
rdctl route update --namespace=streaming --fallback=legacy --ttl=30m
```

sam: good call. We'll leave it on until end of business review.

emily: customer update: "Issue mitigated; latency reduced. We're monitoring and will follow up with postmortem."

mike: any lasting risk? Could the rollout system have bad weighting logic?

jake: root cause looks like a weighting bug in the rollout service: when affinity thresholds cross a shard hotness hysteresis boundary, it over-applied weights to locality. Essentially a double-counting of hot signals during concurrent rollouts.

lia: I've captured traces and stack samples for impacted shards. Will upload to shared folder: https://rbw.infra/trace/6177770000.

mitra: immediate action items: 1) revert rollout (done) 2) temp fallback (done) 3) patch rollout service to prevent double-count of hot signals 4) add canary tests for affinity rollouts that simulate streaming long-seq workloads

sam: assign owners: jake -> rollback & rollout fix PR, lia -> telemetry retention + trace collection, mitra -> fallback TTL and hotkey thresholds, emily -> customer comms and post-incident notes.

jake: creating PR now: "rl: prevent double-count hot-signal accumulation". link: https://git.re/redwood/rollout/pull/5423

incident-bot: Incident declared SEV2 at 09:25 UTC. Bridge remains open for 1h.

mike: moving to handoff in 25m for next oncall. I'll post a short handoff summary to the oncall channel. any other urgent asks?

lia: add regression alert on p99 > 1.5s combined with streaming-error-rate > 0.5% to prevent silent recurrence.

emily: capturing customer A/B ids and impact windows for billing/credit review.

sam: thanks all — postmortem to follow. I'll start the timeline doc and link traces.

mike: :thumbsup: great job. closing bridge in 40m if stable.

incident-bot: Update: p99 = 0.98s, p95 = 0.32s, streaming-error-rate = 0.03%. Monitoring continues.

jake: note: we should add a canary that replays long-seq streaming to new policies before full rollout. Filing ticket: https://app.jira.red/INC-1921

mitra: +1. Also propose a knob to limit per-policy max weight delta per 60s to avoid sudden hot shifts.

emily: will prepare customer-facing RCA draft after postmortem.

sam: last note — link to timeline: https://docs.redwood/incidents/6177770000-timeline (I'll fill)"
